posts.name: Sawyer Merritt
posts.text:
I think AI compute cost-per-watt prices are going to stay elevated a lot longer than many people expect.

Less than 5% of U.S. consumers even pay a subscription for an AI product, with some putting the estimate <2%. People are clearly finding Grok Bot to be very useful because @SpaceX just had to significantly cut back usage capacity due to overwhelming demand. But we're still so early in the AI adoption curve.

Existing users are going to eat up significantly more compute as models get better and agents start handling increasingly complex tasks and jobs. Inference will increasingly become a larger and larger share of compute capacity.

People are seriously underestimating how much demand is still ahead of us and how long it'll take supply to catch up. I think this is partly why Elon thinks SpaceX could exit 2027 with an annual recurring revenue rate of $500 billion to $1 trillion. They can deploy the compute faster than anyone else, and the demand for that compute is insatiable, and likely will be for a long time to come.

In addition, I think supply and demand are closer to being in balance for semiconductors than the companies think given the large inventory growth at their customers. quoted.text:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://hackertube.org/

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

posts.name: Bill Ackman
posts.text:
From a pilot I trust:

It is too early to tell all of the factors that played a roll but likely complacency and inexperience. From the ATC audio tape and radar (see below) I would say inexperienced pilot or pilots and obviously weather. They likely flew into the storms and iced up.  

The Lear has a very critical wing and if they iced up in the thin air at altitude, they likely experienced a power on stall which can result in an upset and or snap roll.  As they asked to climb, we know they were likely at a very high power setting.  

Investigation should provide more insight as to whether they had the radar on or not and the training records as well as experience levels of the crew and any difficulty they may have had over the years with training. They will
also rebuild their days before the flight looking at any causal factors like fatigue.  

This should not have happened. I have a video of the impact and the plane appears to be intact just before impact. 

We absolutely would not cross a line of storms like that while descending into them.

The global copper market is extremely tight:

China's copper import premium over London Metal Exchange (LME) prices has surpassed $200 per ton, the largest premium on record.

The Yangshan premium, named after a Shanghai port that serves as a major hub for Chinese copper imports, has more than doubled over the last 3 months.

Since the beginning of 2026, this figure has surged +700%.

Furthermore, the premium of spot prices over three-month futures on the LME widened to $217 per ton, the largest since mid-August.

This has been driven by strong Chinese copper demand and domestic inventories falling below typical seasonal levels.

At the same time, expectations of potential US tariffs on refined copper have redirected hundreds of thousands of tons of copper to the US, leaving global inventories heavily concentrated in the country.

The physical copper supply squeeze is far from over.

Had 5 roommates in a 3 br apt.  Ate lousy food out of cans and ate  a ton of peanuts and shit food  at happy hour.  Had credit cards ripped up.  Etc.  

But I learned a ton.  Taught me what was right and wrong about running a business by watching my bosses and their bosses 

Yeah I know. It was much easier then, when inflation was 15 pct and national unemployment was 10 %.  I know I was fortunate when I finally got fired from the store, and had to start my own business with zero cash.   Bill collectors everywhere. 
Even luckier when I found my first customer so I could pay my bills

But I recognize it’s so much harder today.  

Which is why I respect the people who are willing to do what it takes to get started

Hey @grok 

Explain how the one-day Friday selloff in the tech sector ranked historically in tech selloffs in one-day moves based on total tech market cap loss and total capital lost by investors.

posts.name: Steve Burns
posts.text:
One of the most useful things to measure after earnings isn't the size of the gap.

Measure how much of that gap survives.
A stock that gaps 12% and keeps 11% has processed the new information very differently from one that gaps 12% and finishes up 2%.

The announcement creates the gap.
The price action afterward tells you what traders ultimately decided about the move.
